shared_elements: low relief carved on a pale stone slab
horizontal register/band across the upper part filled with repeated small marks or motifs
profile bird head with prominent curved beak
registers separating upper band from main figural field
justification: The most specific correspondence is the layout: a tall pale stone slab whose upper zone carries a horizontal band of small repeated marks, separated by a ruled line from a larger figural field containing profile creatures, including a hook-beaked bird head and plant-like fronds. The biggest difference is execution and density: A is a smoothly modelled, finely incised and internally detailed relief with a symmetrical, balanced single dominant figure, while B is a coarse, blocky, schematic relief with scattered, unevenly scaled animals and no comparable centred composition.
